name: Posts
summary: Turns articles worth sharing into posts that are checked against their source, and books them only when you approve.
author: The JimmyHQ project

feeds.name: posted
feeds.label: Posted
feeds.description: Posts that went out: each one's title, the address of its source and the opening of what was posted. Never your notes or a draft.

tools.name: brands
tools.description: Lists the brands the owner posts for. Each has its name, how it sounds in a line, the times of day it posts, which tool books its posts, and whether it is paused. Not its accounts or any key. Use it to learn what exists; the owner's words are shown as written.

limit.description: How many brands to list, from 1 to 25. Leave it out for 10.

tools.name: queue
tools.description: Lists posts the owner approved that have not gone out yet. Each has the brand, where it stands in words (queued, being booked, booked, unsure, missing or failed), the time it is for, and the text to be posted. Latest time first. Not drafts still waiting for approval, and not what went out already.

limit.description: How many posts to list, from 1 to 25. Leave it out for 10.

brand.description: Only this brand's posts: its number, as brands lists it. Leave it out for every brand.

tools.name: went_out
tools.description: Lists posts that went out lately, newest first. Practice posts are left out, since nothing was sent for them. Each has the brand, when, the text posted, and the figures the scheduler reported for it (likes, comments and so on, added up) when it reported any. Not accounts, and not what is still waiting to go out.

limit.description: How many posts to list, from 1 to 25. Leave it out for 10.

brand.description: Only this brand's posts: its number, as brands lists it. Leave it out for every brand.

tools.name: recent
tools.description: Lists what a brand posted lately and what is still being worked on. It includes your own proposals and what became of them, so you do not propose the same thing twice. Leave out page to list the brands and their numbers.

page.description: The brand's number. Leave it out to list the brands with their numbers.

tools.name: what_did_well
tools.description: Shows evidence of what went well on a brand. It gives the owner's approvals, declines and their reasons, and the scheduler's figures when it has any. It says so plainly when there are none. Evidence, never a rule.

tools.name: propose
tools.description: Proposes an article for a brand, with its angle and why the brand's followers would care. Posts reads the article itself and checks it against what the brand covered lately before anyone writes; you are told if it is held as too close. Give url, or article for one Posts has read already.

url.description: The article's address, starting with https://. Posts reads it itself.

article.description: Instead of url: the number of an article Posts has read already, as recent lists it.

angle.description: One or two sentences: what the post would say that is worth saying.

why.description: Why this brand's followers would care, with the evidence you have.

tools.name: brief
tools.description: Gives everything needed to write one piece. It holds the brand's voice and samples, the owner's notes, the researcher's angle, lessons from the owner's past decisions, the checks the code will run, and the article's numbered sentences in pages. Call it again with start to read on.

piece.description: The piece's number, from your task.

start.description: The first sentence number to show. Leave it out to start at the beginning.

tools.name: my_past
tools.description: Shows the writer's last drafts for a brand, so the next one reads differently. For each: how it opened, its shape and its length.

tools.name: submit_draft
tools.description: Hands back a draft, to be checked against its source. Each claim names the numbers of the source sentences it rests on; links are article numbers and Posts writes the addresses. Every check runs at once and you are shown the results. ready=false keeps the draft with you to improve; leave it out to hand it on.

piece.description: The piece's number, from your task.

title.description: A short title for the owner's list. It is not posted.

body.description: The post as it would go out: plain text, no Markdown, no web addresses.

claims.description: One claim per line, each ending with the sentence numbers it rests on in brackets, such as: 1,240 homes added panels last year [2]. Or a JSON list of {"text", "sentences"}. Empty when there is no article.

links.description: The numbers of the articles to link, such as "1". Article 1 is the piece's source. Empty for no link.

ready.description: false to keep working on it after seeing the checks; true or left out to hand it on to be checked.

tools.name: review_packet
tools.description: Gives everything needed to check one draft. It holds its exact text, each claim with the source sentences it cites beside it, the code's own check results, the owner's notes, and the article's numbered sentences in pages. Call it again with start to read on.

piece.description: The piece's number, from your task.

start.description: The first sentence number to show. Leave it out to start at the beginning.

tools.name: submit_review
tools.description: Hands back a review of a draft: ship it or revise it, with points. Each point quotes the draft word for word and names the source sentence it concerns, or says none supports it. Points that do neither are set aside and you are told which.

piece.description: The piece's number, from your task.

verdict.description: ship when it can go to the owner as it is; revise when a point must be fixed first.

points.description: One point per line: "the draft's exact words" | sentence numbers, or none | the problem in one sentence. Or a JSON list of {"quote", "sentences", "problem"}. Empty when there is nothing to raise.

roles.label: Researcher
roles.purpose: Finds articles worth a brand's followers' time and says why, before anything is written.

roles.label: Writer
roles.purpose: Drafts each post from the article's own sentences, in the brand's voice, different from the last.

roles.label: Checker
roles.purpose: Reads each draft against its source and says what is not supported. Never the writer.

secrets.name: socialbu_key
secrets.label: SocialBu key
secrets.help: Only if you book through SocialBu: copy it from SocialBu's settings, under API for Developers. Practice and By hand need none.

secrets.name: buffer_key
secrets.label: Buffer key
secrets.help: Only if you book through Buffer: create a key on Buffer's API settings page (publish.buffer.com/settings/api) and copy it here. Practice and By hand need none.

settings.label: Book through (the default)
settings.help: The default: each brand uses it unless it chooses its own on the Brands screen. Practice books nothing. By hand lists each post with its time, and you press Posted. SocialBu and Buffer book on the accounts listed on the brand, and need their key; Buffer takes text only for now.

settings.label: Posts a day for each brand
settings.help: Booking refuses another post for a brand on a day that already has this many. 0 means no limit.

settings.label: Book at least this far ahead (minutes)
settings.help: A post is booked only for a time at least this far in the future.

settings.label: Sponsor tag
settings.help: Added at the end of a sponsored post when it is booked, if it is not there already.

settings.label: Model role that drafts
settings.help: Used when no agent holds the writer role, and to describe a brand's voice from its posts.

settings.label: Model role that captions pictures
settings.help: Writes a post from what your model for pictures saw and your notes. The pictures themselves always go to your model for pictures.

settings.label: Model role that checks drafts
settings.help: Should be a different model from the one that drafts, so it does not share its blind spots.

settings.label: Articles Reader offers
settings.help: When Reader is installed. Ideas waits for you to press Start on each. Start by itself begins a piece for each, up to the pieces drafted a day, but only with one brand that is not paused. With two or more it does nothing: each article waits in Ideas for you to choose a brand.

options.label: Put each in Ideas, with Start and Dismiss

settings.label: Look for Reader's articles every (minutes)
settings.help: How often Posts reads what Reader offered since it last looked.

settings.label: Pieces drafted a day
settings.help: How many new pieces may start drafting each day. Others wait for the next day. 0 means no limit.

settings.label: Revisions before you see it
settings.help: How many times a draft may be revised after its check. The code stops it here, not the model.

settings.label: Reasons to decline
settings.help: Start your reason with one of these when you decline a draft. Each decline becomes a lesson for later drafts.

settings.label: Remind me about a waiting draft after (hours)
settings.help: A draft card still waiting after this long gets a reminder note.

settings.label: Agent steps for one piece
settings.help: How many tool calls agents may make on one piece. Past it their tools say the budget is spent and to hand back what they have, and nothing more is given to an agent for that piece.

settings.label: Ask the researcher each day
settings.help: When an agent holds the researcher role, ask it once a day for each brand that has room for another piece.

settings.label: Proposals a day for each brand
settings.help: How many articles agents may propose for one brand in a day. 0 means no limit.

settings.label: When an agent is late
settings.help: Remind first, then tell you: a card with Wait, Finish without agents and Drop. Finish without agents does that step the plain way without asking.

settings.label: Research may wait (hours)
settings.help: How long the researcher may take to propose something for a brand before Posts acts as you chose below.

settings.label: Writing may wait (hours)
settings.help: How long the writer may take to hand back a draft or a revision.

settings.label: Checking may wait (hours)
settings.help: How long the checker may take to hand back a review.

settings.label: Look back for overlap (days)
settings.help: New pieces are compared with this brand's posts booked or sent in this many days, and with pieces still open.

settings.label: Say it is close at
settings.help: Similarity (0 to 1) at which a piece is held with a card before anything is spent on it. Must be below the near-duplicate level.

settings.label: Say it is a near-duplicate at
settings.help: Similarity (0 to 1) at which a draft carries a near-duplicate question. Must be above the close level.

settings.label: Pictures in one piece
settings.help: The most pictures one post can start from. Each is looked at by your model for pictures, one at a time.

settings.label: Delete pictures after (days)
settings.help: A picture is deleted this many days after its post went out, was declined, or its piece was dropped. Its fingerprint is kept, so later pictures can still be compared with it.

settings.label: Sources to treat as weak
settings.help: Web hosts whose articles get a weak-source warning, such as forums or link lists. One host per line; its sub-hosts count too.

settings.label: Story found in your notes at
settings.help: A first-person story in a draft counts as yours when this share of its words is in your notes for the piece. Below it, the draft asks you whether it happened.

settings.label: Single-letter keys
settings.help: On the Drafts view: j and k move, a approves, e edits, s sends back, d declines. Switch this off if single letters get in your way, for example with speech input. Enter and Esc still work.

settings.label: Days in the queue's calendar
settings.help: How many days, from today, the calendar strip above the queue shows.

settings.label: Tell me about a stuck post after (hours)
settings.help: A post that has been unsure, out of step, failed or missing for this long gets one card, so it is not forgotten.

settings.label: Call a booking unsure after (minutes)
settings.help: A booking that has had no answer for this long is shown as unsure. It blocks another try until you check the scheduler and clear it.

settings.label: Most batches of SocialBu's schedule to read
settings.help: SocialBu gives its schedule in batches of about 20 posts. The Scheduled view reads at most this many when you open it or press Refresh, so 10 is about 200 posts. When SocialBu has more, the view says its list was cut short.

settings.label: Check the scheduler every (minutes)
settings.help: How often Posts asks the booking tool what became of booked posts: sent, moved there, failed or gone, and whether an unsure booking is there after all.

settings.label: Wait for the booking tool at most (seconds)
settings.help: A request with no answer in this time counts as no answer: a booking becomes unsure and is never tried again by itself. Picture uploads may take longer, up to JimmyHQ's own limit.

settings.label: Largest picture to upload (MB)
settings.help: A bigger picture is refused before anything is sent. SocialBu itself takes up to about 56 MB; Buffer takes text only for now.

settings.label: Collect how a post did for (days)
settings.help: For this many days after a post goes out, Posts keeps the likes, comments and other figures the booking tool gives for it. 0 means never.

settings.label: A drafting step may take (minutes)
settings.help: A step that has not finished in this time is marked stuck, and the piece says so. Nothing is tried again by itself.

settings.label: Shortest readable source (characters)
settings.help: A source with less text than this stops the piece before any model is asked, with a way to try again.

settings.label: Warn when a source is shorter than (characters)
settings.help: A short source is allowed, with a warning on the draft.

settings.label: Longest source kept (characters)
settings.help: How much of an article's cleaned text is kept and given to the models.

settings.label: Close by shared words at
settings.help: Used only when no embeddings model is set up: the share of three-word runs in common at which a piece is held. Must be below the next one.

settings.label: Near-duplicate by shared words at
settings.help: Used only when no embeddings model is set up. Must be above the close level by shared words.

settings.label: Number rounding allowed (percent)
settings.help: A number in a draft matches the source when it is the source's number rounded to the places the draft writes, or within this percentage of it.

settings.label: Warn when a draft has more numbers than
settings.help: Every number is still checked. This only warns that the post may be hard to read.

settings.label: Words in a recycled run
settings.help: A run of this many words in a row shared with a recent draft counts as recycled.

settings.label: Recycled runs before a warning
settings.help: How many shared runs with one recent draft make a warning.

settings.label: Recent drafts to compare with
settings.help: How many of the newest drafts each draft is compared with for recycled runs.

settings.label: Pictures look alike within (of 64)
settings.help: Each picture is shrunk to a 64-point fingerprint. A picture whose fingerprint differs from one in a recent post in this many points or fewer is said to look like it. Lower is stricter.

settings.label: Look for late agents every (minutes)
settings.help: How often Posts looks for an agent that is late, and asks the researcher for ideas.

settings.label: Characters an agent is shown at once
settings.help: How much one answer from a Posts tool may hold. Longer material comes in pages.

settings.label: Earlier posts shown to agents
settings.help: How many of a brand's recent posts, and of the writer's own drafts, agents are shown so they do not repeat them.

settings.label: Lessons shown to the writer
settings.help: How many of your latest decline reasons, send-back notes and edits each brief carries.

settings.label: Points a checker may raise
settings.help: The most points one review may carry. Further points are set aside.

settings.label: Posts and pieces on the screen
settings.help: How many of the newest posts, and of the newest pieces, the Posts screen lists and searches.

settings.label: Text shown for an older post (characters)
settings.help: Posts that went out or were dropped are listed with this much of their text. Open one to read it all.

settings.label: Posts read to fill in a brand's voice
settings.help: When you press "Fill in from its posts", Posts reads up to this many of the newest posts that went out on the brand's accounts. Their text is shown to your model for the "how it sounds" sentence.
